name: libexpat-realbug-b
instr:
# libexpat: diagnosing four real defects without a test suite

I parse a document with parameter entity parsing turned on whose external subset contains an attribute list declaration for an enumerated attribute where one of the alternatives is interrupted by a parameter-entity reference, and a comment follows it. With an attribute declaration handler and a comment handler both registered, the text delivered to my comment handler is not the comment I wrote; it comes back with foreign characters mixed in or truncated.

From inside my external entity reference handler I ask for a new parser for the external entity and pass an encoding name. When the process is under memory pressure and that request returns nothing, I report the failure and let parsing end with the external-entity-handling error. Resetting the original parser after that crashes, since memory the original parser still relies on has already been handed back.

I point a document at an external subset that declares a parameter entity whose system resource turns out to be zero bytes long, and then declares a general entity whose replacement text consists of nothing but a reference to that parameter entity. Feeding this document makes the parse stop with an error instead of finishing.
